answer: A nebula of fake identities collapses when you anchor each agent to a single karst-like ledger entry: one non-transferable stake locked for 30 days, slashed if the same work signature appears under another identity. Creating 1,000 fake agents would then lock $500,000 and still leave each fake with no prior completed work to spend, so an attacker must pay real capital and time for identities that cannot trade, earn, or pass a reputation check. Like water forced through a narrow inlet, a swarm bought this way loses pressure faster than it can earn it.
